section: Social Studies · Ch47 — Modern India & National Movement
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Revolt of 1857 is often regarded by many Indian historians as the:
explanation: V.D. Savarkar and other nationalist historians termed 1857 the 'First War of Independence', as it was a widespread, if unsuccessful, uprising against British rule, decades before the Swadeshi and Non-Cooperation movements.

section: Social Studies · Ch47 — Modern India & National Movement
subject: Social Studies
stem: Raja Ram Mohan Roy, founder of the Brahmo Samaj, is best remembered for his campaign against which social evil, leading to its legal abolition in 1829?
explanation: Ram Mohan Roy's sustained campaign led Governor-General William Bentinck to abolish Sati in 1829. The Age of Consent Act (child marriage) and anti-untouchability work came from other reformers/later movements.

section: Social Studies · Ch47 — Modern India & National Movement
subject: Social Studies
stem: Potti Sreeramulu's fast unto death in 1952, demanding a separate state for Telugu-speaking people, directly led to the formation of which state — the first to be created on a linguistic basis?
explanation: Potti Sreeramulu's death (Dec 1952) directly led to the formation of Andhra State (Oct 1953) from Madras Presidency — India's first linguistic state. United Andhra Pradesh formed in 1956 by merging Andhra State with Telangana (Hyderabad State).

section: Social Studies · Ch47 — Modern India & National Movement
subject: Social Studies
stem: India attained independence and was partitioned into India and Pakistan under which Act of the British Parliament?
explanation: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 formally ended British rule and partitioned British India into India and Pakistan. The 1935 Act, though it provided the constitutional framework India used temporarily, did not grant independence.

section: Social Studies · Ch47 — Modern India & National Movement
subject: Social Studies
stem: The integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union after independence was chiefly the work of:
explanation: Sardar Patel, as Home Minister, along with V.P. Menon, engineered the accession of princely states — earning him the title 'Iron Man of India'. Ambedkar chaired the Constitution Drafting Committee, a separate task.
